correctness.rationale: Independently expanded the literal six monomials on lines and enumerated zero binary quartics in canonical echelon coordinates over F_5[u]/(u^2+u+1), with nonsquare discriminant 2. The six echelon cells have 25, 9, 4, 0, 1, 1 distinct points. To establish geometric exhaustion independently of the frozen cell bounds, the replay computed the full affine Pluecker chart algebras over F_5 in grevlex, of lengths 26, 26, 28, 28, 26, 26 in pivot order 01,02,03,12,13,23. These opens overlap and their lengths must not be added. In the full charts the Jacobian has a nonzero maximal minor except at the four stated coordinate lines. The local jet quotients at those lines have dimension 2 modulo both the square and the cube of the maximal ideal; hence Nakayama makes its square zero and gives local length two. The known points, weighted by these local lengths and counted in each full chart using the corresponding nonzero Pluecker coordinate, exhaust every chart length. Thus there are no additional geometric points. The global length is 36+4*2=44. Exactly four canonical forms have coefficients in F_5; the remaining 36 lie in F_25 and have Frobenius orbit size two. This gives the claimed point counts and zeta function; nilpotents add no field-valued points.
residual_risks: This verifies the printed equation only, not a differently transcribed or intended model. The Gröbner computations are exact computational evidence, not formal proof-assistant verification.

value.rationale: This is a motivated exact correction to a published example, not an arbitrary quartic computation. It distinguishes the actual geometric support (40), scheme length (44), and arithmetic splitting (4 rational and 18 conjugate pairs), so it supplies precise usable data for anyone reusing the printed model in classification or finite-field computations.
residual_risks: No value claim is made as a correction of any unprinted intended model or as a general quartic line bound.
